packagegui.description: Joins pfSense to an Active Directory domain using Samba winbind.
packagegui.requirements: Samba 4.x with winbind, built for the running pfSense release.
packagegui.faq: See the project README for Squid integration and troubleshooting.
packagegui.name: sambaad
packagegui.title: Samba AD: Domain Membership

field.description: Join the domain and run winbindd. Unchecking stops the daemons but keeps the domain membership, so re-enabling does not require another join.
Interfaces winbindd binds to. Loopback is always added automatically because ntlm_auth and wbinfo need it. Select the interface that reaches your domain controllers.
Full DNS name of the Active Directory domain, for example: example.local
Short NetBIOS domain name, for example: EXAMPLE

IP address or FQDN of a domain controller. Leave empty to discover it through DNS SRV records (_kerberos._tcp, _ldap._tcp). Fill it in when the firewall's resolver does not serve the AD zone -- a common case where the domain name resolves but its SRV records do not. When set, the KDC is pinned in krb5.conf and used for the join.
An account permitted to join computers to the domain. Used only for the join and for creating the Kerberos keytab.
Password for the account above. Stored in config.xml; use a dedicated delegated account rather than Domain Admin where possible.

rid (recommended) derives Unix IDs algorithmically and works against a stock Active Directory. ad requires uidNumber/gidNumber attributes to be populated in the directory (RFC2307); if they are not, no user will map at all.
Lowest Unix ID assigned to domain users and groups.
Highest Unix ID assigned to domain users and groups.
Range for everything outside the joined domain. Must not overlap the domain range.
Upper bound of the default range.
Only needed if this firewall should serve SMB file shares. Domain authentication needs winbindd alone, so leave this off unless you know you want a file server on your firewall.
Samba log verbosity (0-10). Use 1 normally; raise to 3 or above only while troubleshooting, as high levels are very noisy.
Extra lines appended to the [global] section, one per line. Applied verbatim.
